title: U.S. House · New Mexico's 3rd District
area: Northern New Mexico, including Santa Fe, Rio Arriba, Taos and surrounding counties.

context.text: Incumbent Rep. Teresa Leger Fernandez (D), first elected in 2020, ran unopposed in the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary. Martin Ruben Zamora, a Republican member of the New Mexico House of Representatives (District 63) since 2019 who is not seeking re-election to that seat, won the Republican primary unopposed.

candidates.name: Teresa Leger Fernandez
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed.

summary.text: Teresa Leger Fernandez is the Democratic incumbent for New Mexico's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2020. A Yale and Stanford Law graduate, she worked as an attorney and advocate in New Mexico, ran her own Santa Fe law and strategy firm, and served in presidential appointments under Presidents Clinton and Obama before entering Congress. She is seeking a fourth term.

background.text: Born in Las Vegas, New Mexico, in 1959, and describes herself as a 17th-generation New Mexican and part of the state's first Head Start class, according to her official House biography. (Ballotpedia's biography gives the birthplace as Las Vegas, Nevada; her official House biography and the Albuquerque Journal place her in Las Vegas, New Mexico.)
Is the daughter of a New Mexico state senator and a bilingual educator, per the Albuquerque Journal, and grew up in Las Vegas, New Mexico.
Earned a B.A. from Yale University and a J.D. from Stanford Law School.

After law school, worked as an attorney and advocate; her official biography says she won legal cases on voting rights, tribal sovereignty and acequia water protection, and served as an acequia commissioner. It states that she helped secure funding for schools, rural health clinics, broadband, affordable housing and infrastructure as a public interest lawyer.
Worked as counsel and a strategist with Leger Law & Strategy.
Served as a White House Fellow working on housing issues (a Clinton appointee) and as vice chair of the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation (an Obama appointee).

Won the 2020 Democratic primary for the open 3rd District seat against six other Democrats, including state Rep. Joseph Sanchez and author and former CIA officer Valerie Plame, then the general election, succeeding Ben Ray Lujan, who ran for the U.S. Senate. She took office in January 2021 and was re-elected in 2022 and 2024.

In Congress, serves on the House Rules Committee and on the Natural Resources Committee, where she is ranking member of the Subcommittee on Indian and Insular Affairs; she chaired that subcommittee in the 117th Congress, when the STOP Act on trafficking of sacred cultural items passed.

Elected chair of the Democratic Women's Caucus in 2024; co-chairs the National Labs, Rural Broadband and Historic Preservation caucuses and chairs the Head Start to Congress Caucus, according to her official biography. Her biography also lists the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon Fire Assistance Act among her legislative work.

positions.summary: Her House issues page says she strongly supports fully funding and strengthening Medicare, Medicaid and community health centers.
positions.quote: I strongly support fully funding and strengthening Medicare, Medicaid, and our nation’s network of community health centers to make sure everyone can access care.

positions.summary: Her House issues page says she voted for the Inflation Reduction Act, which she describes as the largest action on the climate crisis, investing in clean energy production and manufacturing.
positions.quote: The IRA is the largest action to combat the climate crisis in our nation’s history. It invests in clean energy production and manufacturing right here in the United States and puts us on track to reduce carbon emissions by 40 percent by 2030.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources (Federal Lands; Indian and Insular Affairs subcommittees) and the House Committee on Rules (Legislative and Budget Process subcommittee).

candidates.name: Martin Ruben Zamora
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary unopposed.
candidates.currentRole: Member, New Mexico House of Representatives, District 63 (since 2019; not seeking re-election to that seat)

summary.text: Martin Ruben Zamora is the Republican nominee for New Mexico's 3rd Congressional District. A farmer and rancher who owned several agricultural businesses, he has represented New Mexico House District 63 since 2019 and is not seeking re-election to that seat. He has named the economy, energy, border security and agriculture as his top campaign issues.

background.text: Born on a farm near Clovis, New Mexico, and described by the Albuquerque Journal as a farmer and rancher by birth and by trade.
According to his campaign website as reported by the Albuquerque Journal, he and his wife have owned agricultural businesses across Curry, Torrance and Socorro counties.
First won election to the New Mexico House of Representatives, District 63, in November 2018, narrowly defeating incumbent Democrat George Dodge Jr. by 27 votes, and took office in January 2019.
Re-elected in 2020, 2022 and 2024; the Albuquerque Journal reports he ran unopposed in the last two elections for the seat before announcing his congressional bid.
Committee assignments in the state House have included Agriculture, Acequias and Water Resources and State Government, Elections & Indian Affairs, on which he was ranking member in 2023-2024.

Announced a run for the 3rd District seat in a news release, citing federal campaign finance filings; according to the Albuquerque Journal he announced during the 2026 30-day legislative session that he was leaving office, and Republican Seth Martin is unopposed for the District 63 seat in the general election.

His campaign website describes him as a "conservative Hispano leader" who prioritizes agricultural heritage, high-paying jobs and "cracking down on crime and drug trafficking," and also lists water rights as a top concern, according to the Albuquerque Journal. If elected he would be the second Republican to represent the district since it was created in 1982.

positions.summary: His campaign border page lists ending catch-and-release and mandatory detention for illegal border crossers, plus finishing the border wall and more Border Patrol resources, among his policy priorities.
positions.quote: End catch-and-release and enforce mandatory detention for illegal border crossers

record.text: As a New Mexico state representative, served on the Agriculture, Acequias and Water Resources Committee and the State Government, Elections & Indian Affairs Committee (Ranking Member, 2023-2024); currently serves on both committees for 2025-2026.
Won re-election to New Mexico House District 63 unopposed in the 2024 general election (100%, 6,552 votes).

researchNotes: Sitting-member key floor votes and FEC finance totals for Leger Fernandez are added separately by script. Neither candidate's campaign or official website could be confirmed to yield stated policy priorities within the research budget: Leger Fernandez's house.gov issues pages list topic categories without detailed text, and Zamora has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and his sponsored state legislation was not listed in the fetched Ballotpedia table. researchDepth is basic for both; no positions could be documented against a direct source for either candidate, so the positions array is empty for both. Biography gaps: no education or military information for Zamora was found in the sources loaded, and his campaign website could not be loaded directly (its content is reported via the Albuquerque Journal).
